bumpRationale: Patch, security: full scheduled audit pass. This file, package.json and src/lib/appConfig.js's APP_VERSION had drifted three releases stale (still reading 1.7.9) — module 18 (1.7.10) and a first react-router-dom major-bump audit (1.7.11, opened as PR #174 on 2026-08-31) both shipped without updating it; #174 itself never merged because its two CI runs (Node CI, Deno CI) came back red on GitHub Actions with no corresponding local failure. Re-ran every one of #174's checks fresh in this pass on the same Node 22 the workflow pins (npm ci, lint, typecheck, validate:rls, test, test:permissions, release:gate, build) — all green — so the prior failure reads as CI-runner flake, not a real regression; superseded #174 with this branch rather than trying to resurrect a week-old run. New in this pass: npm audit surfaced 4 additional advisories that appeared since #174 was written (1 high: browserslist unbounded memory growth / crash-via-untrusted-stats; 3 moderate/low: @humanfs/node symlink traversal, fflate infinite loop on malformed ZIP64, postcss-selector-parser AST-recursion DoS) — all transitive devDependencies pulled in by eslint/vite/postcss build tooling, none shipped in the production bundle, all closed by npm audit fix with no major bump and no code change; npm audit now reports 0 vulnerabilities. Also corrected this file's stale architecture.router field (react-router-dom v6 -> v7, from #174's already-verified bump) and the inventory.tests count. No RLS, entity, permission, or route-access code touched this pass. Verified: npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm run build, npm run validate:rls (32 entities), npm run test (276/276), npm run test:permissions (23/23), npm run release:gate, npm audit (0 vulnerabilities) all pass.
previousBumpRationale_1_7_9: Patch: release-metadata catch-up (weekly automated audit, 2026-08-24). Five real modules shipped on main between 2026-08-18 and 2026-08-23 — module 11 (deploy tooling: app-id binding, deploy:site), module 12 (three-way light/dark/system theme switcher replacing module 10's two-state toggle), the npm run test:smoke live-site suite, module 14 (multi-tenant isolation audit, one latent not-live finding), and module 15 (per-app derived signing key for the Mission Control bridge, closing a shared-secret attribution gap) — and none of them bumped package.json, added a CHANGELOG.md entry, or updated this file / src/lib/appConfig.js's APP_VERSION, which was still reading 1.7.5, three releases stale. This bump closes that gap; see CLAUDE.md for each module's own detailed writeup. Also fixed in this round: react-router/react-router-dom 6.30.4 -> 6.30.6 (npm audit fix, lockfile-only) closing GHSA-jjmj-jmhj-qwj2 — the other two react-router advisories need a v6->v7 major upgrade and remain accepted risk, unchanged from every prior audit (client-only SPA, no SSR, no externally-controlled navigation target). USER_MANUAL.md gained its first mentions of the theme switcher, the HistorialCambios page (module 6), and the danger-zone export/deletion-request actions (module 7) — all live, user-facing, previously undocumented. New docs/security-audit-2026-08-24.md. No RLS, entity, permission, or route-access code changed. Verified: npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm run build, npm run test (276/276), npm run test:permissions (23/23), npm run validate:rls (32 entities) all pass.
previousBumpRationale_1_7_8: Patch: portfolio-standard audit (module 10 — dark theme). tailwind.config.js already had darkMode:['class'] and index.css already had a complete .dark token palette (shadcn boilerplate), but nothing ever applied the .dark class — no toggle, no persisted preference, no prefers-color-scheme fallback. New src/lib/ThemeContext.jsx (ThemeProvider/useTheme, localStorage key 'liuma-theme', resolution order stored preference -> prefers-color-scheme -> light), a matching inline pre-mount script in index.html (avoids a flash of the wrong theme before React hydrates — kept in sync with ThemeContext.jsx by hand, each side comments the other), and a new ThemeToggle component wired into both places a user can reach it: SideNav's identity footer (desktop) and CommandPalette's new footer row (mobile — the bottom nav's 4 slots were already all spoken for, so the palette, opened from the same 'Más' tab, is the only mobile-reachable spot). Six pre-existing hardcoded-light spots (PendingApproval.jsx, ContinueAs.jsx, App.jsx's two loading skeletons, Layout.jsx's footer, PageNotFound.jsx) got matching dark: variants. Four more hardcoded bg-white/text-slate spots (LumiChat.jsx, HomeChrome.jsx, WelcomeTrialModal.jsx, SuspendedAccountModal.jsx, AdminHome.jsx's tenant-switcher pill) were checked and left as-is — all sit on brand-color (bg-primary) or semantic-color (bg-destructive) surfaces already theme-aware via CSS custom properties, or are white-on-color overlay/scrim decoration, not themed neutral page surfaces. Verified: npm run lint, npm run build, npm run validate:rls (32 entities), npm test (276/276) all pass. Visually verified with Playwright (Chromium) against a local dev server — /login (role-picker step) and a 404 page, both in dark mode — text contrast, card/border colors all render correctly. Not verified: any authenticated page — not reachable without live Base44 auth in this environment; risk is bounded since those pages already use the same semantic tokens (bg-card, text-foreground, etc.) the .dark palette in index.css was hand-tuned for.
previousBumpRationale_1_7_7: Patch: portfolio-standard audit (module 7 — cuenta y zona de peligro). PermisosRoles.jsx already rendered a 'Danger Zone' spec table (delete/suspend/reset/transfer tenant) but it was read-only documentation with no working action behind it — no data export, no way to request deletion. New base44/functions/exportSchoolData (service role, but every read explicitly filtered by the caller's own school_id, re-derived server-side from their ACTIVE ADMIN UserProfile, never trusted from the request) returns every row the school owns across 23 operational entities as one JSON payload; PermisosRoles.jsx turns the response into a client-side download. 'Solicitar eliminación de la escuela' is deliberately NOT a direct delete — School.delete's RLS requires role:admin (the ACACIA platform owner), so a school's own ADMIN cannot delete their own school via RLS at all, by design — this creates a SupportTicket (category ACCOUNT, priority HIGH) via the existing createSupportTicket helper, which resolveSupportRouting already always routes to the platform owner for an ADMIN's own tickets regardless of category. The pre-existing 4-operation maker-checker spec table (delete/suspend/reset/transfer) is left as-is, now explicitly labeled as a separate, larger, not-yet-built initiative rather than conflated with the new functional card — building that maker-checker system for real is out of scope for this release, same reasoning as when it was first documented as deferred. No RLS or entity change beyond the new function. Verified: npm run lint, npm run build, npm run validate:rls (32 entities), npm test (276/276) all pass.
previousBumpRationale_1_7_6: Patch: portfolio-standard audit (module 6 — in-app version/changelog) found LIUMA had no in-app changelog surface at all, only the repo-root CHANGELOG.md. Added src/lib/appConfig.js (APP_VERSION/RELEASE_DATE) and a new HistorialCambios page (route + routeAccess.js entry + nav entry for all three roles under the existing 'Soporte' group), summarizing recent CHANGELOG.md entries in plain-language Spanish for end users, plus a version stamp footer. No RLS, permission, or entity change — a new read-only page, purely additive.
previousBumpRationale_1_7_5: Patch, critical security fix: completing 1.7.3's module-4 live deploy (base44/entities/*.jsonc → the actual Base44 backend, via update_entity_schema — a repo commit alone never changes runtime RLS) surfaced that Base44's live RLS engine silently drops any sibling key placed alongside "user_condition" in the same rule object — {"data.school_id": X, "user_condition": Y} evaluates as user_condition ALONE, X is discarded. That shape was already the DEPLOYED form of most tenant-scoping rules across this app (not something 1.7.3 introduced), found via update_entity_schema's own validator while pushing 1.7.3's fix live. Scanned all 32 entities: 29 had it, 84 instances total, almost all on the data.school_id tenant-isolation clause — meaning any user matching the role half of the rule (e.g. data.app_role:ADMIN) could read/write across ALL schools, not just their own, on nearly every entity in the app. Same defect class jospabloh/cateqhub's CLAUDE.md documents finding once in one entity (Parish) with a note it was worth checking elsewhere — this is elsewhere, at much larger scale. Fixed by wrapping every such pair as an explicit {"$and": [{"user_condition":...}, {...rest}]} — semantics preserved exactly, nothing narrowed or widened beyond restoring the intended tenant scoping. Two further live-engine constraints surfaced and fixed while deploying: (1) a nested $or directly inside another $or is not evaluated on WRITE rules (create/update/delete) — "the branch silently matches" — fixed by flattening (read rules tolerate nested $or fine, left as-is); (2) the entity-side built-in record id must be addressed as "id", not "_id" — Classroom/School/Student used "_id" and were rejected on redeploy; renamed. All 29 corrected entities deployed live via the Base44 MCP and re-fetched to confirm. Added a permanent guard for the primary defect: scripts/validate-rls.mjs now flags any rule object mixing user_condition with sibling keys (previously silent — this exact shape passed validate:rls for years since it's syntactically valid Mongo-style implicit-AND, just not how Base44's engine actually evaluates it). No entity field, property, or intended-access rule changed — verified per-entity that `properties`/`required` are byte-identical before/after and every fix is a pure re-expression of the same access the original (broken) rule intended. 276/276 tests pass; scripts/validate-rls.mjs passes clean (32 entities, new check included); lint clean; build succeeds.

architecture.runtime: browser (client-side only; no application server) + Base44 backend functions for privileged mutations
architecture.router: react-router-dom v7 (declarative mode: BrowserRouter/Routes/Route/useNavigate/Link — stable across v6->v7)
architecture.enforcementBoundary: base44 Row-Level Security (entity + field-level RLS) in base44/entities/*.jsonc + service-role backend functions in base44/functions/*
architecture.language: JavaScript / JSX (type-checked via jsconfig); Deno TypeScript for backend functions

assistantSkills.note: The sibling claude-skills repo holds 48 generic Anthropic/Claude authoring skills (pdf, xlsx, brainstorming, math-olympiad, ...). They are assistant tooling used to BUILD Liuma — NOT features of the application, not integrated into it, and not listed in the user manual.
